newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Cabinet reshuffle a rumour - Deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Cabinet reshuffle a rumour - Deputy PM.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Tuesday described as speculation newspaper reports about an imminent Cabinet reshuffle.
"The speculation has been there for days, weeks, months, years," said Anwar, who is also finance minister, after opening a stock market seminar on Tuesday.
The Chinese-language Sin Chew Jit Poh daily reported on Saturday that at least three ministers will be dropped from the Cabinet under the reshuffle.
The story, picked up by The Sunday Times in neighbouring Singapore, said Anwar was likely to lose his powerful finance minister's job to International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz.
Anwar refused to comment on the details of the reshuffle as speculated by the newspapers.
"That is the sole perogative of the prime minister and I think the media has taken it up from time to time...every other week it will surface," Anwar said.
The ringgit was lower on Monday morning as the speculation spread, while share prices on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange closed firmer on Monday.
"I think the (stock) market should remain bullish and not entertain rumours and speculation," said Anwar.
